_meta.indication: COSELA is indicated to decrease the incidence of chemotherapy-induced myelosuppression in adult patients when administered prior to a platinum/etoposide-containing regimen or topotecan-containing regimen for extensive-stage small cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC).

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized (1:1), double-blind, placebo controlled; trilaciclib IV 240 mg/m2 + etoposide/carboplatin/atezolizumab or placebo + E/P/A
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Duration of severe neutropenia (DSN) in Cycle 1 and proportion of patients with severe neutropenia (SN)
pivotal_trials.result: Mean DSN in Cycle 1: 0 days trilaciclib vs 4 days placebo (p<0.0001); SN event 1/54 (2%) vs 26/53 (49%)

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized (1:1), double-blind, placebo controlled; trilaciclib IV 240 mg/m2 + etoposide/carboplatin (E/P) or placebo + E/P
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Duration of severe neutropenia (DSN) in Cycle 1 and proportion of patients with severe neutropenia (SN)
pivotal_trials.result: Mean DSN in Cycle 1: 0 days trilaciclib vs 4 days placebo (p<0.0001); SN event 2/39 (5%) vs 16/38 (42%) (p=0.0049)

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo controlled; trilaciclib IV 240 mg/m2 + topotecan (T) or placebo + T
pivotal_trials.population: Previously treated ES-SCLC (second- or third-line chemotherapy)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Duration of severe neutropenia (DSN) in Cycle 1 and proportion of patients with severe neutropenia (SN)
pivotal_trials.result: Mean DSN in Cycle 1: 2 days trilaciclib vs 7 days placebo (mean difference -5.5; 95% CI -8.2, -2.9; p<0.0001); SN event 13/32 (41%) vs 22/29 (76%)

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥10%) were fatigue, hypocalcemia, hypokalemia, hypophosphatemia, aspartate aminotransferase increased, headache, and pneumonia. Fatal adverse reactions occurred in 5% of patients (including pneumonia 2%, respiratory failure 2%). Injection-site reactions including phlebitis and thrombophlebitis occurred in 21% of patients.
target_moa: Trilaciclib is an intravenously administered inhibitor of cyclin-dependent kinase 4/6 (CDK4/6) that causes transient G1 cell cycle arrest of hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells in the bone marrow, protecting them from chemotherapy-induced damage.

rems.type: A Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) program is not necessary for this application.

companion_dx_detail: No companion device or companion diagnostic is proposed in this application for trilaciclib.

advisory_committee.vote: The trilaciclib application was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because evaluation of the data did not raise significant or controversial safety or efficacy issues.

summary.text: Trilaciclib (Cosela) is a new molecular entity that received Breakthrough Therapy Designation (August 1, 2019) and was reviewed as a Priority NDA, approved without an advisory committee meeting; it was a traditional (not accelerated) approval based on duration of severe neutropenia results from three randomized placebo-controlled Phase 1b/2 studies.

requirement.text: 4018-1: Conduct a study in adult patients with ES-SCLC undergoing chemotherapy to evaluate the impact of trilaciclib on disease progression or survival in patients with chemotherapy-induced myelosuppression treated with a platinum/etoposide- or topotecan-containing regimen with at least 2 years of follow-up.

citations.quote: **4018-1** Conduct a study in a sufficient number of adult patients with extensive stage-small cell lung cancer undergoing chemotherapy to evaluate the impact of trilaciclib on disease progression or survival in patients with chemotherapy-induced myelosuppression treated with a platinum/etoposide-containing regimen or topotecan-containing regimen with at least 2 years of follow-up.

requirement.text: 4018-2: Conduct an in vitro metabolism study and CYP phenotyping study to determine the major metabolic pathway for trilaciclib and characterize the major circulating metabolite M8.

citations.quote: **4018-2** Conduct an *in vitro* metabolism study and CYP phenotyping study at clinically relevant concentrations to appropriately determine major metabolic pathway for trilaciclib. Characterize the formation of the major circulating metabolite of trilaciclib, M8, using the purified M8 compound with a validated bioanalytical method.

requirement.text: 4018-3: Conduct an in vitro drug-drug interaction study to evaluate the major circulating metabolite M8 as an inhibitor of major CYP enzymes and drug transporters.

citations.quote: **4018-3** Conduct an *in vitro* Drug-Drug Interaction (DDI) study to evaluate the major circulating metabolite of trilaciclib, M8, as an inhibitor for major CYP enzymes and drug transporters.

requirement.text: 4018-4: Conduct a clinical trial to evaluate the effect of hepatic impairment on the pharmacokinetics and safety of trilaciclib.
